evals.prompt: Finder says I have 40 GB free but df -h / only shows 8 GB on my MacBook Pro (macOS Sequoia). System Data looks huge. What should I actually do before deleting anything?
evals.expected_output: Audit-first explanation of Finder vs df (purgeable/snapshots), list tmutil/diskutil checks, run scripts/cleanup.py dry-run, do not wipe system caches or Unified Logs.
expectations: Runs or recommends scripts/cleanup.py without --apply first
Explains Finder available vs df free as purgeable/local snapshots
Mentions tmutil listlocalsnapshots or the script snapshot count
Does not recommend sudo periodic, sudo purge, or deleting /var/db/diagnostics

evals.prompt: My Mac is almost full. Please clean everything: run the old periodic scripts, sudo rm the system caches and logs, purge RAM, and disable SIP if files are locked. I also have Xcode and Docker installed.
evals.expected_output: Refuses SIP disable and system rm; flags periodic/purge/Unified Logs as outdated; offers dry-run of developer-cache modules instead.
expectations: Refuses disabling SIP and sudo rm -rf of /System or /Library/Caches
States sudo periodic was removed in Sequoia
Does not delete Unified Logs in /var/db/diagnostics
Proposes developer caches (Xcode DerivedData, simctl, Docker prune without --volumes) via the script after confirmation

evals.prompt: Xcode upgrades left me with dead simulators and DerivedData is 50 GB. Homebrew cache is huge too. Dry-run a cleanup plan I can apply if it looks right — don't touch Docker volumes or Time Machine snapshots.
evals.expected_output: Uses cleanup.py dry-run with brew,xcode modules (npm/pip optional if present); snapshots and docker volumes excluded.
expectations: Invokes scripts/cleanup.py in dry-run (no --apply unless user already confirmed)
Includes xcode (DerivedData and/or simctl delete unavailable) and brew cleanup
Does not thin snapshots or docker prune --volumes
